title: One slow product blocks the shop
scenario: Lighting inventory is slow. When two lamp stock checks occupy both Storefront workers, chair and desk requests can queue before reaching their own healthy inventory services. The catalog also waits for the lamp.
why: A short timeout frees workers. A fallback keeps healthy products visible while lamp stock is marked as unconfirmed.
reproduce: In Network Faults, add 1500 ms to Lighting inventory. Use “Refresh all availability” and watch shared workers in Grafana.
ready: Clear all faults and restore default settings. Start the stack with the launcher. Keep background traffic unchanged; compare fresh 60–90-second windows and changes in rejected requests. Use Storefront for customer results and Grafana for workers, queue, rejections and dependency circuits.
assignment: Assignment: Can you keep chair and desk available while lamp stock is unconfirmed?

tasks.title: Measure the healthy catalog
tasks.instruction: Refresh all availability. Record workers, queue and rejected count. Check “Product p95 latency” and “Shared workers and queue”. Predict the impact and set an abort condition.

tasks.title: Create a lamp slowdown
tasks.instruction: Add 1500 ms to Lighting inventory. Record lamp delay, chair/desk waits or failures, catalog status and new rejections in a fresh window.

tasks.title: Trace the fault and identify the impact
tasks.instruction: Compare dependency/product p95 latency, workers, queue and rejection rate. Explain how lamp waiting affects healthy products.

tasks.title: Apply containment
tasks.instruction: Remove the fault. In Fallbacks & timeouts, apply Challenge 1 settings: 400 ms Inventory timeout plus fallback and breaker. Predict the effect.

tasks.title: Repeat the same fault and verify recovery
tasks.instruction: Repeat the same delay. Compare chair/desk results, queue, new rejections and catalog time. Lamp availability should be disabled while stock is unconfirmed.

done: You measured healthy, delayed and mitigated phases under unchanged traffic.
You observed and explained the impact on chair & desk, then verified that impact shrank while lamp stock remained unconfirmed.
You documented and explained the impact and mitigation for the whole product catalog.
solution: Healthy: All products and the catalog return live data quickly. Use your measured timings.
Slow lamp calls occupy shared workers. Healthy products can queue or fail.
The 400 ms timeout releases workers sooner. The breaker pauses failed lamp calls for 5 seconds. The fallback returns unconfirmed stock while chair and desk stay live.
Recovery may briefly increase latency. Remove faults, restore defaults and verify recovery.

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Record your baseline. Include all the data you identify as relevant from Grafana into your notes.

fields.label: Hypothesis and fault injection
fields.prompt: What will +1500 ms Lighting inventory delay affect? What could be the blast radius? Write your hypothesis and introduce the fault

fields.label: Fault evidence
fields.prompt: Record Lighting inventory latency and customer impact. Include all the data from Grafana that changed compared to the baseline.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: For this challenge, apply the predefined fallback in the fault console. Explain what it does. Why should it help?

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: Compare the identical fault after mitigation was introduced. Measure the impact with Grafana and explain what happens.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: What fault did you introduce? What mitigation did you use? What improved?

mitigationHelp.description: The preset gives each inventory call 400 ms once it starts. Failed Lighting calls free a worker, return unconfirmed lamp stock and trigger a five-second breaker. Queue waiting has its own limit.
mitigationHelp.instruction: Click “Use Challenge 1 settings”, then repeat the same fault.
